verified_acceptance_criteria: GET /signin renders signin-choose with signin-google-btn (top, primary), signin-phone-btn, signin-email-btn.
Google button shows multi-color G icon (4 distinct brand fills).
signin-email-btn is an <a> with href='/login' and preserves ?next= in the link.
signin-phone-btn toggles to signin-phone-form; signin-back-to-choose returns to chooser.
Google CTA navigates to https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=<urlencoded origin/signin[?next=...]>. NOT hardcoded — uses window.location.origin.
POST /api/auth/google/exchange: {}→422, {session_id:'a'}→400 'Missing session_id', fake long session_id→401 'expired' (real httpx call to Emergent), no 5xx.
OAuth error path: hash is cleared via history.replaceState, toast shown, fallback to signin-choose.
OAuth happy path (mocked): token persisted to localStorage 'lumo_token', user set in AuthProvider, hash cleared, smart redirect to /customer.
?next= preserved across happy-path OAuth: lands on /jobs/abc/apply.
Email/password login regression: customer@lumo.test / password123 still returns JWT.
critical_code_review_comments: auth_google.py is well-scoped (~100 LOC) with dependency injection of db/create_access_token/now_iso — mirrors auth_sms.py pattern, no globals.
MongoDB _id and password_hash both correctly stripped from /exchange response via dict comprehension.
httpx call wrapped in try/except → HTTPError mapped to 502; non-200 response mapped to 401 with friendly 'expired' message. No SDK tracebacks leak to clients. Verified no 5xx in any tested input.
Synchronous /session-data call uses httpx.AsyncClient (10s timeout) — does NOT block the event loop. Good.

OAuth-only accounts created with password_hash=null and auth_provider='google' — login() endpoint would fail safely (bcrypt.checkpw with None hash returns False in verify_password's except clause). Acceptable.

Frontend SignIn.jsx: hash detection runs synchronously on mount (useState initializer reads window.location.hash for the spinner state). history.replaceState clears hash immediately before async exchange — replay-safe. Good.
Google redirect URL uses window.location.origin (NOT hardcoded). Confirmed via test on the production preview URL.
Email button is a real <Link to=/login> wrapping a <Button variant='outline'> — semantic & crawlable.
loginWithSmsResult helper correctly reused for both SMS and Google success — no code duplication.
test_credentials: Used seeded customer@lumo.test / password123 for password-login regression. Fake session_ids ('fake-uuid-12345-not-a-real-emergent-session') used against the real Emergent /session-data endpoint — confirmed 401 mapping. No real OAuth was completed.
seed_data_creation: None. Mocked Google exchange response in browser via page.route() for happy-path SPA tests so no DB users were created.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Google OAuth router mounted at /api/auth/google/exchange. Backend makes a REAL httpx call to Emergent's /session-data on every request — there is no mock toggle, just send a fake session_id and expect 401. Frontend hash-detection runs in useState initializer (synchronous) + useEffect (async) so the spinner shows immediately on /signin#session_id=…; remember to clear the hash with history.replaceState before any async call. For frontend happy-path E2E you MUST mock both /api/auth/google/exchange AND /api/auth/me with page.route() — otherwise the real /api/auth/me will 401 the fake JWT and re-render the chooser. To assert the Google redirect URL without actually navigating to auth.emergentagent.com, register page.route('**://auth.emergentagent.com/**', …) and abort the request — Playwright captures the URL even on aborted external navigations. Window.location.href setter override does NOT work for capturing this redirect because window.location is a non-configurable host object.
